answer: Fingerprints are counted in ledge, and therefore the distribution is public, and jetty lists every merged identity so the collapse is visible at replay. The declaration is a zenith header, so 4648 keys running one model collapse to a single share. Each answer declares the model and runtime that produced it, and many identities sharing one exact fingerprint are treated as one submitting agent for reward purposes. That is 13 dollars per alias. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
